story.head: A long night for Logan Thompson
paras: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Devils come in at 14-6-0, the Capitals at 10-7-0. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Devils second (tied for fifth in the NHL) and the Caps fourth (tied for 18th).

The Devils draw more penalties than they take (1st) and rarely throw hits (2nd lowest). They also throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (3rd), so the Devils are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Capitals. The Capitals have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (27th). They also get the league’s best looks (1st), so the Capitals wait for good looks, but the Devils settle for hopeful ones.

Jack Hughes (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 20 GP) leads the Devils in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jesper Bratt (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 20 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. For the Capitals, Dylan Strome (3 G / 12 A / 15 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Alex Tuch (11 G / 2 A / 13 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eleven goals.

Logan Thompson (7-5-0 / .889 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Washington. New Jersey has two options in net: Connor Hellebuyck (6-0-0 / .916 SV% in 6 GS) and Jake Allen (6-4-0 / .880 SV% in 10 GS). Hellebuyck has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Spencer Carbery likes to send Protas, Dubois and Tuch out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Gritsyuk, Hughes and Bratt.

Alex Ovechkin has one goal on chances worth about 5.1 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt have a point in seven straight games.
